title: Bug
description: One bug in the app under test, in bugs/<ID>.yml, one per root cause. Scenarios that hit it name it with bug (next to knownIssue). Key order: id, title, status, severity, layer, area, affects, found, resolved, ref, upstream, description, steps, expected, actual, evidence.

id.description: Bug ID with the prefix and digits from simpright.yml (ids.bugs), e.g. BUG-001; the file is named after it.

title.description: One line naming the wrong behaviour: what happens instead of what should.

status.description: open: still in the app; fixed: the app was fixed (the scenarios drop knownIssue); wont-fix: accepted as is.

severity.description: critical: security or data loss; major: a feature or rule doesn't work, or a server error; minor: wrong but with a workaround or little impact; trivial: cosmetic.

layer.description: Where the defect is, a layer from the profile's ids.layers (api, ui). Scenarios of any layer can name the bug.

area.description: An area from the profile's ids.areas.

affects.description: The endpoints (GET /products/{productId}/related) or pages (/product/{id}) that show the bug.

found.description: Date the bug was found, YYYY-MM-DD.

resolved.description: Date the status changed to fixed or wont-fix, YYYY-MM-DD. Required unless the status is open.

ref.description: Where the expected behaviour comes from: a contract section, a user story criterion, a source file. One or a list.

upstream.description: Link to the bug in the app's own tracker, when it was reported there.

description.description: Optional: the impact and, when known, the cause in the app's code.

steps.description: Steps to reproduce, in order. No secret values: write "the default user's email", not the address.

evidence.description: Optional: the request and response, or a run link, masked like the reports (no tokens, passwords or test users' emails).
